blocks.heading: Choose your next version
blocks.body: Choose a specific arrangement before starting. The cards below offer a reflective piece, a cheerful programme option, a familiar theme, an intermediate solo and an accompaniment resource.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] editorial guidance using verified version metadata

blocks.heading: Sad or reflective
blocks.body: Gymnopédie No. 1 is our reflective selection because the publisher describes long phrases and wide bass-to-chord spacing. “Sad” is an editorial listening lens; it is not an objective property of every performance.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] selection guidance; version facts verified in listed sources

blocks.heading: Happy, cool or fun
blocks.body: The Happy Farmer is a cheerful-title selection. Addams Family Theme is a theme-song choice for a playful programme. Their appeal depends on your audience and preferences.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] selection guidance; version facts verified in listed sources

blocks.heading: Beautiful
blocks.body: For a spacious, reflective goal, audition the selected Gymnopédie. Choose the sound you want to work on; this is not a beauty ranking.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] selection guidance; version facts verified in listed sources

blocks.heading: Intermediate
blocks.body: The Gymnopédie edition is late intermediate and calls attention to long phrases and bass-to-chord spacing. Empire State of Mind is in an explicitly intermediate piano-solo collection; inspect its own sample before comparing the two.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] selection guidance; version facts verified in listed sources

blocks.heading: Types of piece
blocks.body: The catalogue includes an étude route on the challenging page, a fantasy there, soundtrack tracks such as Sweden, simplified classical excerpts and songs arranged for singing. These labels help you choose a playing task.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] selection guidance; version facts verified in listed sources

blocks.heading: Sing and play
blocks.body: All of Me has a vocal line and piano part with guitar chord frames. Start there when you need singing support; choose the Easy Songs page for a melody-first solo task.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] selection guidance; version facts verified in listed sources

blocks.heading: Open the exact edition
blocks.body: Each resource names its edition and access route. Publisher difficulty labels describe that arrangement. Use the provider’s preview before purchasing; check the chosen digital format before expecting a printable PDF.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] acquisition guidance

blocks.heading: Choose an easy version you can actually use
blocks.body: Start with the arrangement, not just the song title. The featured choices below identify a specific score or lesson and explain the next thing to check. Publisher labels such as Early Elementary and Easy Piano come from different series; treat them as starting points for comparing the actual music.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] 编辑选择方法；依据所列出版方采用不同级别标签

blocks.heading: For a child’s first few pieces
blocks.body: Hot Cross Buns comes with first-lesson materials and a parent guide. The early-elementary Twinkle version adds a hand-position graphic and a matching tutorial. For a birthday goal, the early-elementary Happy Birthday divides the melody between the hands. Choose the version and lesson together.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] 版本功能；儿童起步选择为[推断]

blocks.heading: If you want a C-major version
blocks.body: The listed early-elementary Twinkle, Jingle Bells and Happy Birthday editions are in C major. The selected Ode to Joy arrangement is in D major, so it is outside this filter. A key name alone does not describe the rhythm, hand movement or reading work.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] 调性；难度比较建议为[推断]

blocks.heading: For adult beginners
blocks.body: If you follow Alfred’s adult course, compare The Rainbow Connection or Nadia’s Theme in its Greatest Hits Book 1 with your current lesson. If you want a broader menu, the edition-backed list offers fifty titles from one Easy Piano collection. Those are purchased arrangements, not fifty free downloads or fifty individually tested recommendations.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] 版本归属；选择为[推断]

blocks.heading: For a gentle piece or a small performance
blocks.body: For a gentle option, compare the two Twinkle arrangements and listen to their separate samples. For a small performance, choose a meaningful occasion: Happy Birthday gives you a clear audience and purpose. “Beautiful” and “impressive” describe your goal here; neither is a guaranteed listener response.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] 主观编辑选择，依据标注Dreamily与生日场合；不承诺效果

blocks.heading: Before you commit
blocks.body: Open the exact resource, check how to obtain it, and try a short section at a comfortable pace. Prefer a version whose instructions you understand. Several free provider downloads request your name and email. For a printed copy, check the chosen format: an online digital book and a downloadable PDF are different products.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] 编辑操作建议；获取方式已核实

/keyboard-notes.title: Piano Keys and Notes: Find Any Key
/keyboard-notes.description: Identify a piano key, locate a note by octave and compare verified 88-key and 61-key example ranges.
/keyboard-notes.user_task: Identify one key or find a named pitch without guessing its octave.
questions: What is this piano key called?
Where are F3, A4, A5 and C3?
Which octave do C and A-flat refer to?
How many white/black keys and octaves are in the chosen layout?
Which black key is next to G?
Where are B-sharp and C-flat, including octave boundaries?
Is D8 included?

blocks.heading: Find a piano key or note
blocks.body: Choose a keyboard layout, then select a key to see its note name and octave. To find a note from its name, enter a full label such as F3 or A4. A letter alone, such as C, identifies several keys; choose an octave before selecting one. Use Play note when you want to hear the selected pitch.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Page interaction copy applying the confirmed lookup task and the verified distinction between pitch class and pitch.

blocks.heading: Read the repeating pattern
blocks.body: The white-key letters repeat A, B, C, D, E, F, G. Black keys form groups of two and three. Find C just before a two-black-key group, and F just before a three-black-key group. Between one C and the next C are twelve semitone steps; the upper C begins the next repeat.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Summary and direct keyboard-position deductions from verified naming and grouping rules.

blocks.heading: How many keys and octaves?
blocks.body: The standard 88-key layout shown here runs from A0 to C8: 52 white keys and 36 black keys. Its lowest-to-highest span is seven octaves plus three semitones. The alternative 61-key example runs from C2 to C7, spanning five octaves with 36 white and 25 black keys. Check your instrument’s endpoints before using that example.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Endpoints and 88-key count independently verified; 61-key counts and exact interval spans counted from the complete checked key arrays.

blocks.heading: Black keys, sharps and flats
blocks.body: A black key can have two familiar names: C♯/D♭, D♯/E♭, F♯/G♭, G♯/A♭, or A♯/B♭. These pairs point to the same piano key. Sharps and flats can also name white keys. The black key to the left of G is F♯/G♭; the one to its right is G♯/A♭.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Which C, A or F?
blocks.body: This reference calls middle C C4. C3 is one octave below it; A5 is one octave above A4. F3 is the F in octave 3. An A-flat query keeps the name A♭ while offering its matching octaves. For staff positions, open the notes chart; for A4 or another note in hertz, open the frequency table.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Examples follow the verified octave-label rule; internal links follow the frozen URL plan.

blocks.heading: Keep spelling and range visible
blocks.body: B♯3 shares the C4 key; B♯4 shares C5. C♭4 shares B3, not B4. Keep the written name and its octave together. D8 lies above this 88-key layout’s C8 endpoint. An out-of-range result should stay visible as a message, rather than moving the requested note to another octave.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: B#3 and Cb4 examples explicitly sourced; neighboring examples and out-of-range state calculated from the same verified rules and endpoints.

/keyboard-notes/labeled.title: Labeled Piano Keys: 88-Key and 61-Key References
/keyboard-notes/labeled.description: Match letter and octave labels to a defined 88-key or 61-key layout, with clear steps for labeling your keyboard.
/keyboard-notes/labeled.user_task: Choose an accurate labeling reference matching the keyboard endpoints and prepare a readable print reference.
questions: Which 88-key or61-key labeling diagram matches my instrument?
How do octave suffixes distinguish repeated letters?
Where do labels start on a C2–C7 61-key keyboard?
How can I label real keys using the black-key groups?
Is the printout a reference or a full-size sticker template?

blocks.heading: Choose the layout that matches your keyboard
blocks.body: Start with the 88-key reference, A0–C8, or select the 61-key example, C2–C7. Both use letter names and an optional octave suffix, with middle C labeled C4. The 61-key chart describes this specific range; a key count alone does not establish the labels of every keyboard model. Compare the leftmost and rightmost notes with your instrument.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Read letters and octave labels
blocks.body: The white keys repeat C–D–E–F–G–A–B within each numbered octave. Turn octave labels on to distinguish C3 from C4, or A4 from A5. The black-key labels show familiar sharp/flat pairs, such as F♯/G♭. An octave number identifies the note’s register; it is not a finger number or a scale degree.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Label a small section first
blocks.body: First locate a group of two black keys and find the C immediately before it. Match that C to the correct octave in the reference. Next, label the following white keys D, E, F, G, A and B. Check the three-black-key group above F, G, A and B before continuing. Add the sharp/flat names only after the white-key labels match.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Original step order built from verified keyboard landmarks and note naming; no claim about a superior learning method.

blocks.heading: Where to start on the 61-key example
blocks.body: For the C2–C7 layout, label the leftmost white key C2. Continue through B2, then begin C3, and repeat until the final C7. This layout has six C keys but spans five C-to-C octaves. On the A0–C8 layout, the first three keys are A0, A♯0/B♭0 and B0 before C1. Do not begin that layout with C.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Step-by-step labeling and counts derived from the verified endpoints and complete ordered key data.

blocks.heading: Print a reference you can read
blocks.body: Choose the same layout and octave-label setting for screen and print. Use the marked octave sections to read a long keyboard in smaller pieces. The printout is a reference diagram, not a full-size sticker template. If you use physical labels, match each one to the verified key before applying it and follow the label and instrument instructions for placement.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Editorial instructions within the confirmed reference-print and physical-labeling task; dimensions, adhesives and manufacturer compatibility have not been established.

blocks.heading: Match the note to the key
blocks.body: Start with middle C, labeled C4 here. It is one ledger line below the treble staff and one ledger line above the bass staff. Both spellings point to the same piano key. The clef changes where that pitch is written; it does not create a different middle C.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Treble clef: read from the bottom
blocks.body: The five treble-staff lines are E4, G4, B4, D5, and F5, read upward. The four spaces are F4, A4, C5, and E5. The curl of the clef identifies the G4 line. Use that anchor and the repeating musical alphabet to find nearby notes.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Bass clef: a different set of positions
blocks.body: The bass-staff lines are G2, B2, D3, F3, and A3. Its spaces are A2, C3, E3, and G3. The two dots surround the F3 line. A note in the bottom space is therefore A2 in bass clef, while the bottom treble space is F4.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Follow the lines beyond the staff
blocks.body: Ledger lines extend the same line-and-space sequence. D4 lies just below the treble staff without a ledger line; C4 uses the first ledger line below it. Above bass clef, B3 needs no ledger line, and C4 uses the first one. Keep octave numbers visible when comparing notes with the same letter.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Choose the range shown on your keyboard
blocks.body: The full-piano view uses the standard 88-key range A0-C8. The 61-key view here uses C2-C7, a layout documented by VOX and Roland. Check your instrument’s endpoints and transpose setting before using that view. A key-count setting changes the visible keyboard range; it does not rename the clefs.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Try one note in both directions
blocks.body: Select C4 on the staff, then locate its highlighted key. Next, select G4 on the keyboard and read its treble position. Compare C3 with C4 to check the octave. For black keys, compare a sharp and a flat spelling while keeping the same physical key selected. Use the selected range for a readable printout.

content.heading: How to read this piano chord chart
paragraphs: A dot marks a key to play. The labels identify those pitches; a sharp (♯) raises a written note by one semitone, and a flat (♭) lowers it by one semitone.

C4 means middle C. The number after a note is its octave, not a finger number. The diagrams use the same C3–C5 window so you can compare positions. A note such as C♭4 keeps the octave of its written C even though it uses the B3 key.
steps: Read the chord name and its note list. A symbol such as Am names the root A and the minor chord type.
Match the marked keys to the labels. Notes are listed from lowest to highest.
Use Play chord to hear the notes together, or Play notes one at a time to hear the same notes in ascending order.
Compare the keyboard image with the printed note list before playing it on your instrument.

content.heading: Major and minor: change the third
paragraphs: A major triad places its third four semitones above the root. A minor triad places its third three semitones above the root. Both use a perfect fifth, seven semitones above the root.
In the A examples, C♯ becomes C while A and E stay in place. In the C examples, E becomes E♭ while C and G stay in place. The note names in the tables are chord members, not finger numbers.

rows: Are these all the chords on piano?
No. This chart covers nine named major and minor triads. Seventh chords, power chords, jazz voicings, and a complete set of roots are not included in this collection.
What are the 12 chords for piano?

There are 12 semitone pitch positions in an octave in equal temperament. A root can support more than one chord type, so “12 chords” does not mean there are only 12 chords on a piano. Check which chord type a chart is listing.
Does the PDF show finger positions?
It shows which keys to play, with note and octave labels. It does not give finger numbers.
Why do B major and C-flat major use the same keys?
They are enharmonic spellings in this keyboard reference. B major is B–D♯–F♯; C-flat major is C♭–E♭–G♭. Keep the spelling shown by the chord you are reading.

rows: Is Am the same as A minor?
Yes. Am is a common chord symbol for the A minor triad. You may also see A min or A−.
Does Am/C become a C chord?
No. It is still A minor, with C as the lowest note. Its chord tones are still A, C, and E.
Is Am the same as Am7?
No. Am is A–C–E; Am7 adds G. This page covers the three-note Am chord.
Are the numbers in A3, C4, and E4 finger numbers?
No. They identify octaves. The diagrams in this reference do not prescribe fingering.

blocks.heading: Piano scales: choose a sound, then a starting note
blocks.body: Start with C major: C–D–E–F–G–A–B–C. Choose another tonic to compare its notes. The final C repeats the first note one octave higher; it is not an eighth distinct scale degree.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Read the pattern
blocks.body: For a major scale, move by whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half steps. A whole step spans two adjacent-key steps; a half step spans one. Keep the note spelling shown for the chosen key. Fifteen conventional major-key spellings in this chart represent twelve tonic pitch classes on an equal-tempered keyboard.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] 由核实音程及本表15行音高类集合计算

blocks.heading: Choose the minor form
blocks.body: A natural minor uses A–B–C–D–E–F–G. Harmonic minor raises G to G♯. Classical melodic minor raises F and G on the way up and returns to the natural-minor notes on the way down. Select the form before comparing, listening, or printing.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Same notes or same tonic?
blocks.body: C major and A natural minor share a note collection but organize it around different tonics. C major and C minor start on the same tonic; C natural minor lowers E, A and B to E♭, A♭ and B♭.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Give each note a job
blocks.body: In C major the degrees are C tonic, D supertonic, E mediant, F subdominant, G dominant, A submediant and B leading tone. In natural minor, degree seven is a whole step below the tonic and is called the subtonic.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A few jazz scale examples
blocks.body: Compare C Dorian (C D E♭ F G A B♭), C Mixolydian (C D E F G A B♭), and C blues (C E♭ F G♭ G B♭). Bebop dominant adds a major seventh to Mixolydian; C B B♭ A G F E D C gives a descending example. The choice of notes still depends on the musical context.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Continue with a different type
blocks.body: Use the modes page to compare seven diatonic modes. Pentatonic and blues pages show their own note collections. Chromatic practice moves through every neighboring key. Harmonic major has its own reference page; it is not another name for harmonic minor.

/scales/c-major.title: C Major Piano Scale: Notes and Fingering
/scales/c-major.description: See C major notes, key signature, keyboard pitches and separately verified one-octave fingering for each hand and direction.
/scales/c-major.user_task: Find the C-major notes and learn the first one-octave hand crossing without confusing scale degrees with finger numbers.
questions: What are the notes and key signature of C major?
Why are E–F and B–C closer in pitch even though the scale uses only white keys?
Which fingers are used by each hand ascending and descending over one octave?
What should I check during a short practice run?

blocks.heading: C Major notes
blocks.body: C Major contains C, D, E, F, G, A, B. Repeat C at the top to complete one octave. Its key signature has no sharps or flats.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: White keys, unequal distances
blocks.body: C major uses only white keys, but those keys are not equally spaced in pitch. E–F and B–C are half steps; the other adjacent pairs in the scale are whole steps. Keep that distinction when checking the keyboard against the staff. Beginning on another white key does not preserve the C-major tonic.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Explanatory relationships derived from independently checked note spelling and the verified major-scale interval rule.

blocks.heading: One-octave fingering
blocks.body: In this one-octave version, the right hand crosses from E with finger 3 to F with the thumb. The left hand crosses from G with the thumb to A with finger 3. Read the separate descending row when coming back. Finger numbers identify the fingers, not the scale degrees.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A short practice check
blocks.body: Suggested drill: play C–D–E, pause, then continue F–G–A–B–C with the printed right-hand fingers. Next, connect E–F without the pause. With the left hand, isolate G–A instead. Finish with one unhurried ascent and descent, saying each note name.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Original suggested drill using only the source-verified notes and explicit fingering for this key. No effectiveness or fixed learning-time claim.

intervals.basis: Apply the verified major-scale interval rule to the independently checked note spelling. Descending order follows the same pitches from upper tonic to lower tonic.

display_register.RH: tonic written in octave 4 to tonic written in octave 5
display_register.LH: tonic written in octave 3 to tonic written in octave 4
display_register.basis: Editorial display choice; octave labels follow MusicXML C4=middle C; each accidental remains attached to its written octave. This register choice is not asserted to be a source-prescribed exercise range.

pitch_sequences.basis: MIDI = 12*(written_octave+1)+natural_letter_pitch_class+alter; computed from verified spelling. Cb4=59, equivalent to B3, not B4.

fingering.source_locator: LearnMusicTheory PDF page 1 C major row; Music Fun PDF page 3 staff
fingering.variant_note: A source-documented single-octave choice, not a claim that no alternative fingering is valid. Do not extend to multiple octaves by repeating these rows.
fingering.direction_evidence: Both ascending and descending notes and finger numbers were read directly in each displayed source staff; descending arrays were not merely assumed from an ascending-only source.

renderer_payload.tempo_status: editorial playback default; not a sourced examination speed or promised learning target
renderer_payload.source_of_truth: pitch_sequences plus same-hand fingering rows; no automatic enharmonic respelling

/scales/a-minor.title: A Minor Scale on Piano: Natural, Harmonic & Melodic
/scales/a-minor.description: Find the notes of A minor, compare its three forms and descending patterns, and read source-checked piano fingerings.
/scales/a-minor.user_task: 直接查看指定调性的音阶、键位、手别指法和示范。
questions: What notes are in A natural minor?
Which notes change in A harmonic and melodic minor?
What is the descending classical melodic-minor sequence?
Which fingers are supported for each hand and range?
How do I match the keyboard, score and printed note names?
Which chords use the A natural minor scale?

blocks.heading: Start with A natural minor
blocks.body: A natural minor uses A, B, C, D, E, F, and G. Its key signature has no sharps or flats. C major shares that signature, but A is the starting note and tonal reference here. The all-white-key description applies to natural minor; it does not describe every form of A minor.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Listen for the changed ending
blocks.body: Harmonic minor replaces G with G#. Classical melodic minor uses F# and G# on the way up, then F and G on the way down. Keep the form label visible when comparing the examples: a descending melodic scale is not simply the ascending note list played backward.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Practice the last four notes
blocks.body: Try E-F-G-A first, then E-F-G#-A, then E-F#-G#-A. Say the changed note names before playing each group. Next, start at the upper A and return through G-F-E. Keep this a note-recognition exercise; choose your own slow pace and pause between forms. Finish by naming which version you just played.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.inference_basis: 本站编辑练习/实现建议；根据已核实的本调音名、上下行规则或明确指法行设计，未声称练习效果经实验验证。

blocks.heading: Connect the scale to chords
blocks.body: The natural-minor triads are Am, Bdim, C, Dm, Em, F, and G. Compare Em with E major: E major contains G#, matching the raised seventh in A harmonic minor. Use the existing A minor chord reference for voicing and inversions; this scale page focuses on which notes the chords draw from.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

pitch_mapping.basis: Arithmetic from verified note spelling and semitone rules; C4=MIDI60 convention from AN-BMT-AS. Display octave is an editorial choice, not a sourced performance prescription.

/guide/read-sheet-music.description: Connect the clef, staff position, key and duration before you play.
/guide/read-sheet-music.user_task: Decode a short score and identify notes in the correct register.
questions: How do clefs map to keys?
Where does FACE apply?
What does two ledger lines below mean?

blocks.heading: Read in a useful order
blocks.body: Identify the clef first. Read the key signature and any accidental beside the note, then locate the note on a line or space. Finally read its duration. A higher position on a staff means a higher written note; alternating lines and spaces move through successive letter names.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Use anchors, then count steps
blocks.body: In treble clef, the second line from the bottom is G4. In bass clef, the fourth line is F3. Middle C, C4, is on the first ledger line below treble or above bass. These two written positions represent the same piano key.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: FACE has a specific job
blocks.body: F4–A4–C5–E5 names the four spaces inside the treble staff, from bottom to top. It does not name the bass spaces. For “two lines below,” first identify the clef: the second ledger line below treble is A3; below bass it is C2.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Check yourself
blocks.body: Name the first ledger-line note below treble, then the next two staff positions upward. Answer: C4, D4, E4. Find them on the keyboard and play the first bar of Steps around middle C. The printable shows both the notation and an answer key.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

exercise.goal: One staff, C4–F4, steps and one third, quarter/half/whole notes; no simultaneous hands.

blocks.heading: Read the tuning label first
blocks.body: This chart uses twelve-tone equal temperament with A4 set to 440 Hz. Each semitone has the same frequency ratio, and an octave doubles the frequency. The values are calculated reference frequencies. They are not measurements of an individual piano or a promise about its current tuning.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Find the note and the key
blocks.body: The table runs from A0, piano key 1, to C8, piano key 88. It includes black keys and their common sharp/flat names. Use the piano key number to locate a key from the left end of an 88-key keyboard; use the MIDI number when matching a software note event. These are different numbering systems.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: What is the frequency of C4?
blocks.body: With the stated A440 reference, C4 is approximately 261.63 Hz. It is MIDI note 60 and piano key 40 in this chart. A4 is MIDI note 69 and 440.00 Hz. Frequencies in the visible table are rounded to two decimal places; calculations retain more precision.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

blocks.heading: Check labels when using other software
blocks.body: This page names middle C as C4. Some instruments or programs use a different octave label for the same MIDI number. Check the numeric MIDI value as well as the note name. Changing the reference frequency changes the resulting frequencies, so comparisons must use the same reference.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: How the values are calculated
blocks.body: For MIDI note number m, the reference frequency is f = 440 × 2^((m − 69)/12) Hz. For example, moving twelve semitones above A4 gives A5 at 880 Hz. If a comparison instead assumes A4 = 442 Hz, replace 440 with 442; that is a different reference table.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

/keyboard-notes/finger-numbers.title: Piano Finger Numbers: Left and Right Hand
/keyboard-notes/finger-numbers.description: Learn piano finger numbers 1–5 for both hands and distinguish finger labels from note names and scale degrees.
/keyboard-notes/finger-numbers.user_task: Identify the finger meant by a piano fingering number on either hand and follow the correct specific reference.
questions: Which finger is 1 on the left and right hand?
Why do the two hand diagrams read in opposite directions?
Do finger numbers name piano keys?
How are finger numbers different from scale degrees?

blocks.heading: Both thumbs are 1
blocks.body: Piano finger numbers use the same labels on both hands: thumb 1, index finger 2, middle finger 3, ring finger 4 and little finger 5. The little finger is also called the pinky. LH means left hand and RH means right hand. Start by checking the hand label as well as the number.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Read each hand separately
blocks.body: The diagrams show the backs of your hands as you look down with your fingertips pointing away. The thumbs face inward. From left to right, the left-hand labels read 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, while the right-hand labels read 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The fingers keep their identities when the picture is mirrored.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

blocks.heading: A number identifies a finger
blocks.body: Finger 1 does not permanently mean C. A fingering mark says which finger is intended for that note in that passage. Published exercises can ask the same thumb to play C and then D. For a particular scale, chord or arpeggio, use its own stated hand, direction and range.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Finger numbers and scale degrees
blocks.body: A finger number labels part of your hand. A scale degree labels a note’s position relative to the tonic. Finger 3 means the middle finger; scale degree 3 means the third degree of the scale. Reading one does not tell you the other.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Try a quick identification check
blocks.body: Find the left thumb, then the right little finger. Name their numbers before checking the table. Next find finger 2 on each hand. This check only asks you to identify fingers; choose a specific scale or chord reference when you need instructions for playing notes.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

/keyboard-notes/key-signatures.title: Piano Key Signatures: Major & Minor Chart
/keyboard-notes/key-signatures.description: Look up sharp and flat key signatures, their relative major and minor keys, and what it means to call piano a non-transposing instrument.
/keyboard-notes/key-signatures.user_task: 查调号，并理解钢琴乐器与调性的关系
questions: Which major and minor keys share this signature?
What is the order of sharps and flats?
Does an empty key signature always mean C major?
Are harmonic-minor alterations part of the signature?
What does instrument in C mean for piano?
Which related scale page can I open?

blocks.heading: Read the signature as a pair
blocks.body: The chart lists 15 written major-key signatures and their relative minors, from no accidentals through seven sharps or seven flats. A signature alone does not tell you whether the music is major or minor. For example, two sharps belong to D major or B minor; look at the melody and harmony for the tonal center.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Keep the accidental order
blocks.body: Sharps enter in this order: F#, C#, G#, D#, A#, E#, B#. Flats enter in the reverse letter order: Bb, Eb, Ab, Db, Gb, Cb, Fb. Use the whole row when reading a signature. Six flats include Cb, and seven flats also include Fb; those spellings should not be removed because their piano keys are white.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Separate the key signature from minor-scale changes
blocks.body: C major and A minor both have an empty key signature. A minor may still use G# as a leading tone; that note is written as an accidental when needed. The minor column in this chart names the key, not a promise that every passage uses only the natural-minor collection.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: What key is the piano in?
blocks.body: Piano is a non-transposing instrument: in ordinary notation, a written C sounds as C. Calling it an instrument in C describes this relationship between written and sounding pitch. It does not restrict piano music to C major. For example, a pianist can read an F-major signature with Bb or a D-major signature with F# and C#.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Try the two-sharp example
blocks.body: Select the row for two sharps. Check F# first, then C#, and compare the D-major and B-minor names beside it. Follow an available scale link to see how those notes are ordered from the chosen tonic. Keep enharmonic names visible as separate written choices instead of silently replacing one signature with another.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

/chord-progressions.title: Piano Chord Progressions
/chord-progressions.description: Try complete examples in C, E and A major and compare how they return or repeat.
/chord-progressions.user_task: Choose a progression, inspect every chord and try an original realization.
questions: What is a progression?
What are the actual chords in C, E or A?
Can a progression guarantee a happy or beautiful sound?

blocks.heading: Hear the sequence
blocks.body: A chord progression is an ordered sequence of harmonies. I–V–vi–IV becomes C–G–Am–F in C major, E–B–C-sharp minor–A in E major, and A–E–F-sharp minor–D in A major. The original examples below give a concrete register and four counts per chord.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] source formulas; [推断] original voicings/editorial examples

blocks.heading: Compare three patterns
blocks.body: The collection includes I–V–vi–IV, I–vi–IV–V, and a four-bar I–IV–V–I practice example. Try the first two as loops, then compare the last pattern’s final return to I. The printable includes all three keys and every chord’s notes.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] source formulas; [推断] original voicings/editorial examples

blocks.heading: Explore an effect
blocks.body: For a “beautiful” starting point, try the I–vi–IV–V example slowly, sounding chord tones in sequence. For a “happy” starting point, try the I–IV–V–I example with light, even pulses. These are subjective playing suggestions: neither label is a property guaranteed by the chord order.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] source formulas; [推断] original voicings/editorial examples

/scales/modes.title: Seven Scale Modes on Piano
/scales/modes.description: Compare all seven diatonic modes on C, with notes, interval patterns and related major collections.
/scales/modes.user_task: Compare seven modes with the same tonic, then distinguish parallel modes from relative collections.
questions: What notes are in each mode on C?
Which scale degrees change?
How are parallel modes different from relative modes?
Which example can I compare next?

blocks.heading: Compare seven modes on C
blocks.body: A mode is more than a new starting label. The seven diatonic modes have different arrangements of whole and half steps. Keeping C as the tonic makes those differences easier to compare: the first and last note stay C while selected notes inside the octave change. The table gives one complete C example for every mode.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Find the changing notes
blocks.body: Compare C Ionian with C Lydian: F becomes F-sharp. Compare Ionian with Mixolydian: B becomes B-flat. Within the minor group, C Dorian uses A-natural where C Aeolian uses A-flat. C Phrygian also lowers D to D-flat; C Locrian lowers G to G-flat as well. Read each note list before playing so the altered notes remain visible.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Same tonic or same collection?
blocks.body: Parallel examples share C as their tonic. Relative examples share a pitch collection but have different tonal centers. For instance, C Dorian and B-flat major use the same pitch classes. That relationship helps identify notes; it does not establish that a passage is in C Dorian simply because those notes appear.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

blocks.heading: Try one comparison
blocks.body: Play C Ionian, then C Lydian. Pause on F and F-sharp and return to C after each example. Next compare the A-flat in C Aeolian with the A-natural in C Dorian. Keep the comparison short and use the note lists as your check.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

blocks.heading: Choose major or minor blues
blocks.body: This reference covers two six-note blues-scale forms in C and G. Minor blues adds a note between the fourth and fifth degrees of minor pentatonic. In C, that gives C, E-flat, F, G-flat, G and B-flat. Major blues adds a chromatic note between the second and third degrees of major pentatonic. C major blues contains C, D, E-flat, E, G and A.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Read the blue-note label
blocks.body: The minor examples use the label flat fifth: G-flat in C, D-flat in G. You may also see the same piano keys named sharp fourth. The major examples use flat third for the extra note; some theory texts spell that passing tone as sharp second. Keep the displayed spelling when reading a particular example.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Use the scale as a reference
blocks.body: Minor blues vocabulary can occur over major blues harmony. A major or minor label therefore does not provide a rule that every note will fit every chord in the same way. These note collections are a starting reference; phrasing and the accompanying harmony still matter.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Hear the added note
blocks.body: Compare C minor pentatonic with C minor blues. Play F, G-flat, G slowly, then finish on C. Next compare D, E-flat, E in the C major blues example. Keep the two forms separately labeled so their different thirds do not get mixed together.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

/scales/d-major.title: D Major Piano Scale: Notes and Fingering
/scales/d-major.description: See D major notes, key signature, keyboard pitches and separately verified one-octave fingering for each hand and direction.
/scales/d-major.user_task: Play D major in either direction while preserving F-sharp and C-sharp and the documented hand changes.
questions: What are the notes and key signature of D major?
Do F-sharp and C-sharp stay sharp when D major descends?
Which fingers are used by each hand ascending and descending over one octave?
What should I check during a short practice run?

blocks.heading: D Major notes
blocks.body: D Major contains D, E, F#, G, A, B, C#. Repeat D at the top to complete one octave. Its key signature has 2 sharps.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Keep both sharps through the return
blocks.body: The two sharps are F-sharp and C-sharp. They belong to both directions of this major scale. F♯–G and C♯–D are its half steps. On the staff, the key signature supplies those sharps; on the keyboard, locate the named black keys before beginning.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Explanatory relationships derived from independently checked note spelling and the verified major-scale interval rule.

blocks.heading: One-octave fingering
blocks.body: For the one-octave ascent, the right-hand thumb follows finger 3 from F♯ to G. In the left hand, finger 3 follows the thumb from A to B. The final C♯–D is played with right-hand fingers 4–5 and left-hand fingers 2–1.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A short practice check
blocks.body: Suggested drill: locate F♯ and C♯ without playing the whole scale. Then play D–E–F♯–G and A–B–C♯–D as two listening groups. Join them at the same pulse, turn around at the upper D, and check that neither sharp has become a natural on the descent.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Original suggested drill using only the source-verified notes and explicit fingering for this key. No effectiveness or fixed learning-time claim.

intervals.basis: Apply the verified major-scale interval rule to the independently checked note spelling. Descending order follows the same pitches from upper tonic to lower tonic.

display_register.RH: tonic written in octave 4 to tonic written in octave 5
display_register.LH: tonic written in octave 3 to tonic written in octave 4
display_register.basis: Editorial display choice; octave labels follow MusicXML C4=middle C; each accidental remains attached to its written octave. This register choice is not asserted to be a source-prescribed exercise range.

pitch_sequences.basis: MIDI = 12*(written_octave+1)+natural_letter_pitch_class+alter; computed from verified spelling. Cb4=59, equivalent to B3, not B4.

fingering.source_locator: LearnMusicTheory PDF page 1 D major row; Music Fun PDF page 5 staff
fingering.variant_note: A source-documented single-octave choice, not a claim that no alternative fingering is valid. Do not extend to multiple octaves by repeating these rows.
fingering.direction_evidence: Both ascending and descending notes and finger numbers were read directly in each displayed source staff; descending arrays were not merely assumed from an ascending-only source.

renderer_payload.source_of_truth: pitch_sequences plus same-hand fingering rows; no automatic enharmonic respelling

/scales/e-minor.description: Find the notes of E minor, compare its three forms and descending patterns, and read source-checked piano fingerings.
/scales/e-minor.user_task: 直接查看指定调性的音阶、键位、手别指法和示范。
questions: What notes are in E natural minor?
Which notes change in E harmonic and melodic minor?
What is the descending classical melodic-minor sequence?
Which fingers are supported for each hand and range?
How do I match the keyboard, score and printed note names?

blocks.heading: One sharp stays in place
blocks.body: E natural minor contains E, F#, G, A, B, C, and D. The key signature has F#, and its relative major is G major. F# stays in all three minor forms shown here. The changing notes are near the end of the octave, rather than at the opening F#.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Compare C and D carefully
blocks.body: E harmonic minor has D# while C remains natural. Classical melodic minor raises both C and D on ascent, giving C# and D#. Its descent returns through D and C, with F# still present. Keep these two jobs separate: retaining the key-signature F# and tracking the altered sixth and seventh degrees.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A focused listening exercise
blocks.body: Play E-F#-G and stop. Then move to B-C-D-E, B-C-D#-E, and B-C#-D#-E as three separate endings. Name each ending before you play it. Try a descending check from the upper E and identify whether you selected natural, harmonic, or classical melodic minor. Review any changed note individually before repeating the full octave.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.inference_basis: 本站编辑练习/实现建议；根据已核实的本调音名、上下行规则或明确指法行设计，未声称练习效果经实验验证。

blocks.heading: Use the fingering that matches the example
blocks.body: For the sourced one-octave natural and harmonic ascents, the right hand begins 1-2-3 on E-F#-G and continues with the thumb on A. The left-hand row begins with finger 5 on the lower E. Read the selected form and direction before following a numbered row; missing rows remain unavailable until reviewed.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

/scales/f-major.title: F Major Piano Scale: Notes and Fingering
/scales/f-major.description: See F major notes, key signature, keyboard pitches and separately verified one-octave fingering for each hand and direction.
/scales/f-major.user_task: Find F major’s B-flat and use its specific right-hand fingering rather than copying C major.
questions: What are the notes and key signature of F major?
Why does the right hand use finger 4 on B-flat?
Which fingers are used by each hand ascending and descending over one octave?
What should I check during a short practice run?

blocks.heading: F Major notes
blocks.body: F Major contains F, G, A, Bb, C, D, E. Repeat F at the top to complete one octave. Its key signature has 1 flat.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: B-flat changes the right-hand crossing
blocks.body: F major contains B-flat, with A–B♭ and E–F as the half-step pairs. Write B♭, rather than A♯, in this scale: each scale degree keeps its own letter name. The one-flat key signature applies in both ascending and descending notation.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Explanatory relationships derived from independently checked note spelling and the verified major-scale interval rule.

blocks.heading: One-octave fingering
blocks.body: The documented right-hand ascent is 1–2–3–4–1–2–3–4: finger 4 plays B♭, then the thumb plays C. The left hand uses 5–4–3–2–1–3–2–1. The right hand therefore ends this single octave on finger 4, not finger 5.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A short practice check
blocks.body: Suggested drill: with the right hand, practice A–B♭–C–D using 3–4–1–2, then return using 2–1–4–3. Add the surrounding notes only after you can follow those numbers without stopping. In the left hand, check the separate C–D crossing before joining the hands.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Original suggested drill using only the source-verified notes and explicit fingering for this key. No effectiveness or fixed learning-time claim.

intervals.basis: Apply the verified major-scale interval rule to the independently checked note spelling. Descending order follows the same pitches from upper tonic to lower tonic.

display_register.RH: tonic written in octave 4 to tonic written in octave 5
display_register.LH: tonic written in octave 3 to tonic written in octave 4
display_register.basis: Editorial display choice; octave labels follow MusicXML C4=middle C; each accidental remains attached to its written octave. This register choice is not asserted to be a source-prescribed exercise range.

pitch_sequences.basis: MIDI = 12*(written_octave+1)+natural_letter_pitch_class+alter; computed from verified spelling. Cb4=59, equivalent to B3, not B4.

fingering.source_locator: LearnMusicTheory PDF page 1 F major row; Music Fun PDF page 10 staff
fingering.variant_note: A source-documented single-octave choice, not a claim that no alternative fingering is valid. Do not extend to multiple octaves by repeating these rows.
fingering.direction_evidence: Both ascending and descending notes and finger numbers were read directly in each displayed source staff; descending arrays were not merely assumed from an ascending-only source.

blocks.heading: G Major notes
blocks.body: G Major contains G, A, B, C, D, E, F#. Repeat G at the top to complete one octave. Its key signature has 1 sharp.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: The last step is F-sharp to G
blocks.body: The seventh degree is F-sharp, not F natural. F♯–G is a half step; the other half step is B–C. A run of white keys from G to G would therefore miss one of the notes required for G major. The single sharp remains present on the way down.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Explanatory relationships derived from independently checked note spelling and the verified major-scale interval rule.

blocks.heading: One-octave fingering
blocks.body: The right hand changes from finger 3 on B to the thumb on C, then reaches F♯ with finger 4. In the left hand, the thumb on D is followed by finger 3 on E. These are separate crossing points even when both hands move upward.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A short practice check
blocks.body: Suggested drill: play E–F♯–G, then G–F♯–E, keeping F♯ in both directions. Next, start the full scale from the lower G and name the two half-step pairs as you reach them. Use the descending finger row rather than restarting the ascending row from the top.

/scales/pentatonic.title: Pentatonic Scales on Piano: Major and Minor
/scales/pentatonic.description: See five pentatonic examples, compare major and minor forms, and find their notes on the keyboard.
/scales/pentatonic.user_task: Compare the five-note major and minor pentatonic collections using concrete piano examples.
questions: Which five notes belong to major and minor pentatonic?
How do C major and C minor pentatonic differ?
Why do C major and A minor pentatonic share notes?
Which notes are omitted from the seven-note scale?

blocks.heading: Five different notes
blocks.body: Pentatonic means five tones. This page focuses on the common major and minor forms. Major pentatonic keeps degrees 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 of the major scale. Minor pentatonic keeps 1, flat 3, 4, 5 and flat 7. Repeating the starting note at the octave completes the exercise without adding a sixth pitch class.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Compare the same tonic
blocks.body: C major pentatonic contains C, D, E, G and A. C minor pentatonic contains C, E-flat, F, G and B-flat. They share C and G, but the remaining notes change. Use this pair when the question is how major and minor pentatonic differ on the same root.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Compare related collections
blocks.body: C major pentatonic and A minor pentatonic share their five pitch classes, ordered around different tonics. G major pentatonic and E minor pentatonic make another related pair. These comparisons explain shared notes; they do not make the two tonic labels interchangeable in a musical passage.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

blocks.heading: Try a short note check
blocks.body: Read C major pentatonic upward and return to C. Then read C minor pentatonic and name the three changed notes. For a second check, find the same five keys used by C major pentatonic and A minor pentatonic, starting and ending on the named tonic each time.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

/scales/a-major.title: A Major Piano Scale: Notes and Fingering
/scales/a-major.description: See A major notes, key signature, keyboard pitches and separately verified one-octave fingering for each hand and direction.
/scales/a-major.user_task: Translate the three-sharp A-major key signature into the correct ordered piano notes.
questions: What are the notes and key signature of A major?
Why is F-sharp first in the key signature when C-sharp comes first in the scale?
Which fingers are used by each hand ascending and descending over one octave?
What should I check during a short practice run?

blocks.heading: A Major notes
blocks.body: A Major contains A, B, C#, D, E, F#, G#. Repeat A at the top to complete one octave. Its key signature has 3 sharps.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Read all three sharps
blocks.body: A major uses C-sharp, F-sharp, and G-sharp. In the key signature, their written order is F♯, C♯, G♯; in the ascending scale, C♯ is encountered first. The half-step pairs are C♯–D and G♯–A. Key signatures list accidentals in a fixed order; a scale lists notes starting from its tonic.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Explanatory relationships derived from independently checked note spelling and the verified major-scale interval rule.

blocks.heading: One-octave fingering
blocks.body: For this one-octave version, the right hand crosses from C♯ with finger 3 to D with the thumb. The left hand crosses from E with the thumb to F♯ with finger 3. The final G♯–A uses right-hand fingers 4–5 and left-hand fingers 2–1.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A short practice check
blocks.body: Suggested drill: point to the three altered notes in the note list, then play A–B–C♯–D followed by E–F♯–G♯–A. During a return run, say G-sharp and F-sharp aloud. Finish by checking the same passage on the staff without adding unnecessary accidental symbols beside every note.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Original suggested drill using only the source-verified notes and explicit fingering for this key. No effectiveness or fixed learning-time claim.

intervals.basis: Apply the verified major-scale interval rule to the independently checked note spelling. Descending order follows the same pitches from upper tonic to lower tonic.

display_register.RH: tonic written in octave 4 to tonic written in octave 5
display_register.LH: tonic written in octave 3 to tonic written in octave 4
display_register.basis: Editorial display choice; octave labels follow MusicXML C4=middle C; each accidental remains attached to its written octave. This register choice is not asserted to be a source-prescribed exercise range.

pitch_sequences.basis: MIDI = 12*(written_octave+1)+natural_letter_pitch_class+alter; computed from verified spelling. Cb4=59, equivalent to B3, not B4.

fingering.source_locator: LearnMusicTheory PDF page 1 A major row; Music Fun PDF page 6 staff
fingering.variant_note: A source-documented single-octave choice, not a claim that no alternative fingering is valid. Do not extend to multiple octaves by repeating these rows.
fingering.direction_evidence: Both ascending and descending notes and finger numbers were read directly in each displayed source staff; descending arrays were not merely assumed from an ascending-only source.

renderer_payload.source_of_truth: pitch_sequences plus same-hand fingering rows; no automatic enharmonic respelling

questions: What notes are in C natural minor?
Which notes change in C harmonic and melodic minor?
What is the descending classical melodic-minor sequence?
Which fingers are supported for each hand and range?
How do I match the keyboard, score and printed note names?

blocks.heading: Find the three-flat starting point
blocks.body: C natural minor uses C, D, Eb, F, G, Ab, and Bb. Its signature contains Bb, Eb, and Ab, shared with Eb major. Keep Eb as the third degree in every minor form on this page. Changing the upper part of the scale does not turn that Eb into E.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: B natural changes the harmonic form
blocks.body: The harmonic version replaces Bb with B natural and retains Ab. Ascending classical melodic minor uses A natural and B natural; descending it returns to Bb and Ab. Compare the spelling as well as the sound. The B in harmonic minor is a raised seventh degree, not an extra note added between Bb and C.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Separate the opening from the ending
blocks.body: First play C-D-Eb-F-G, then stop. Continue with Ab-Bb-C for natural minor, Ab-B-C for harmonic minor, or A-B-C for melodic ascent. Return to the upper C before testing each descent. For a written check, label the sixth and seventh degrees in all three versions and circle only the notes that change.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.inference_basis: 本站编辑练习/实现建议；根据已核实的本调音名、上下行规则或明确指法行设计，未声称练习效果经实验验证。

blocks.heading: Keep the register and direction together
blocks.body: The one-octave ascent rows below are kept separate from the additional two-octave natural-minor demonstration. Use one complete row for its stated range. A continuous two-octave run passes through the middle C and ends only at the top C, so its middle and ending finger choices are not interchangeable.

questions: What notes are in D natural minor?
Which notes change in D harmonic and melodic minor?
What is the descending classical melodic-minor sequence?
Which fingers are supported for each hand and range?
How do I match the keyboard, score and printed note names?

blocks.heading: Begin with the B-flat
blocks.body: D natural minor contains D, E, F, G, A, Bb, and C. Its one-flat signature is shared with F major. Bb belongs to this starting collection. Keep the note spelling visible when locating it on the keyboard so that it remains the sixth degree of D minor.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A flat and a sharp can appear together
blocks.body: D harmonic minor keeps Bb and changes C to C#. In ascending classical melodic minor, Bb also rises to B natural. The descending melodic version uses C and Bb again. The form selector therefore changes specific scale degrees; it does not apply a rule that every note must use only flats or only sharps.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Compare three routes back to D
blocks.body: Try A-Bb-C-D, then A-Bb-C#-D, then A-B-C#-D. Leave a short pause after the final D and say the name of the form. Next, play down from the upper D using the displayed descending row. Before restarting, check whether the next sixth degree is Bb or B natural.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.inference_basis: 本站编辑练习/实现建议；根据已核实的本调音名、上下行规则或明确指法行设计，未声称练习效果经实验验证。

blocks.heading: Check the transition before a full run
blocks.body: For the sourced natural and harmonic one-octave ascents, the right-hand third finger plays F before the thumb moves to G. Practice that small connection slowly, then add the selected ending. The left-hand row has its own sequence. Do not transfer a right-hand crossing instruction to the left hand.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

/scales/e-major.description: See E major notes, key signature, keyboard pitches and separately verified one-octave fingering for each hand and direction.
/scales/e-major.user_task: Navigate E major’s four black keys while keeping the white-key anchors and hand crossings visible.
questions: What are the notes and key signature of E major?
Which notes remain natural in the four-sharp key of E major?
Which fingers are used by each hand ascending and descending over one octave?
What should I check during a short practice run?

blocks.heading: E Major notes
blocks.body: E Major contains E, F#, G#, A, B, C#, D#. Repeat E at the top to complete one octave. Its key signature has 4 sharps.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Use E, A, and B as visual anchors
blocks.body: The unaltered note names in E major are E, A, and B. F♯, G♯, C♯, and D♯ fill the remaining degrees. Its half steps are G♯–A and D♯–E. Both involve a black key followed by a white key in the ascent.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Explanatory relationships derived from independently checked note spelling and the verified major-scale interval rule.

blocks.heading: One-octave fingering
blocks.body: The right-hand thumb moves from its initial E to A after fingers 2 and 3 play F♯ and G♯. The left-hand thumb reaches B, then finger 3 crosses to C♯. On the descent, use the separately recorded reverse-direction fingers attached to the notes.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A short practice check
blocks.body: Suggested drill: locate E, A, and B first, then fill in the intervening scale notes. Play G♯–A and D♯–E separately and listen to each half step. Finally, run from E to E and back while checking that the four sharp names survive the change of direction.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Original suggested drill using only the source-verified notes and explicit fingering for this key. No effectiveness or fixed learning-time claim.

intervals.basis: Apply the verified major-scale interval rule to the independently checked note spelling. Descending order follows the same pitches from upper tonic to lower tonic.

display_register.RH: tonic written in octave 4 to tonic written in octave 5
display_register.LH: tonic written in octave 3 to tonic written in octave 4
display_register.basis: Editorial display choice; octave labels follow MusicXML C4=middle C; each accidental remains attached to its written octave. This register choice is not asserted to be a source-prescribed exercise range.

pitch_sequences.basis: MIDI = 12*(written_octave+1)+natural_letter_pitch_class+alter; computed from verified spelling. Cb4=59, equivalent to B3, not B4.

fingering.source_locator: LearnMusicTheory PDF page 1 E major row; Music Fun PDF page 7 staff
fingering.variant_note: A source-documented single-octave choice, not a claim that no alternative fingering is valid. Do not extend to multiple octaves by repeating these rows.
fingering.direction_evidence: Both ascending and descending notes and finger numbers were read directly in each displayed source staff; descending arrays were not merely assumed from an ascending-only source.

renderer_payload.source_of_truth: pitch_sequences plus same-hand fingering rows; no automatic enharmonic respelling

blocks.heading: Keep C-sharp and F-sharp
blocks.body: B natural minor uses B, C#, D, E, F#, G, and A. Its two-sharp signature is shared with D major. C# and F# remain present in each version here. G and A are the degrees to watch when switching between natural, harmonic, and melodic minor.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: The raised seventh is A-sharp
blocks.body: B harmonic minor replaces A with A# while leaving G natural. Ascending classical melodic minor uses G# and A#. Its descending form restores A and G. The last step into the upper B is therefore A#-B in harmonic minor and melodic ascent, while natural minor uses A-B.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Start each hand from its own row
blocks.body: In the sourced one-octave natural and harmonic ascents, the left hand starts with finger 4 on B. Its first four notes use 4-3-2-1; the right-hand row starts with the thumb. This distinction matters when changing hands. Check the hand label before rehearsing the notes or marking a printed copy.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Practice one fixed opening and two changing notes
blocks.body: Play B-C#-D-E-F# and pause. Add G-A-B, G-A#-B, or G#-A#-B. Name the ending you chose, then try the other versions without changing the opening. Finish by reading the selected descending notes out loud before playing them. Keep the exercise short enough that you can identify every accidental without guessing.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

blocks.heading: Read the four-flat collection
blocks.body: F natural minor contains F, G, Ab, Bb, C, Db, and Eb. Its signature is shared with Ab major. The four flats are Bb, Eb, Ab, and Db. In all forms here, Ab and Bb remain in the lower part of the scale; the sixth and seventh degrees distinguish the versions.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: E natural replaces E-flat
blocks.body: F harmonic minor changes Eb to E natural while keeping Db. Ascending classical melodic minor uses D natural and E natural. Descending melodic minor restores Eb and Db. Read those natural signs as changes to the key-signature pitches when you compare the written forms.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Watch the right-hand ending
blocks.body: The sourced one-octave natural and harmonic ascents use right-hand fingers 1-2-3-4-1-2-3-4. The thumb moves to C after finger 4 on Bb, and finger 4 ends on the upper F. Keep this row with its one-octave example; do not replace its ending with a memorized five-finger finish.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Use a small comparison task
blocks.body: Start with F-G-Ab-Bb-C, then pause. Add Db-Eb-F, Db-E-F, and D-E-F in separate attempts. Before the melodic descent, name Eb and Db again. On a printed note list, underline Ab and Bb as the unchanged lower notes and mark the two upper degrees separately. Replay only the ending you misread, then return to the full octave.

/scales/harmonic-major.title: Harmonic Major Scale on Piano
/scales/harmonic-major.description: Compare C and G harmonic major with their major scales, including the lowered sixth and augmented second.
/scales/harmonic-major.user_task: Identify harmonic major, compare it with major and harmonic minor, and read C/G examples.
questions: What changes from the major scale?
What are the notes in C and G harmonic major?
Where is the augmented second?
How is harmonic major different from harmonic minor?

blocks.heading: Major with a lowered sixth
blocks.body: Harmonic major keeps the major third and major seventh of a major scale while lowering its sixth degree. Its formula is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, flat 6, 7. C harmonic major therefore uses A-flat in place of the A-natural found in C major. The remaining C-major note names stay the same.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Read two concrete examples
blocks.body: C harmonic major contains C, D, E, F, G, A-flat and B. G harmonic major contains G, A, B, C, D, E-flat and F-sharp. The G example retains F-sharp: lowering the sixth changes E, not the seventh. Compare the major and harmonic-major rows before following the keyboard sequence.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Notice the larger step
blocks.body: The gap from the lowered sixth to the seventh spans three semitones: A-flat to B in C, or E-flat to F-sharp in G. With those letter spellings, the interval is an augmented second. Harmonic minor also contains this gap, but its third degree is minor; harmonic major retains the major third.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

blocks.heading: Compare one changed note
blocks.body: Read G major once, then G harmonic major. Isolate D, E-flat, F-sharp, G and check the written accidentals. Repeat the comparison on C using G, A-flat, B, C. Keep the spelling visible rather than renaming A-flat as G-sharp.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

/scales/a-sharp-minor.title: A# Minor Scale on Piano: Natural, Harmonic & Melodic
/scales/a-sharp-minor.description: Find the notes of A# minor, compare its three forms and descending patterns, and read source-checked piano fingerings.
/scales/a-sharp-minor.user_task: 直接查看指定调性的音阶、键位、手别指法和示范。
questions: What notes are in A# natural minor?
Which notes change in A# harmonic and melodic minor?
What is the descending classical melodic-minor sequence?
Which fingers are supported for each hand and range?
How do I match the keyboard, score and printed note names?
Why are B#, E#, F## and G## retained instead of respelling the key?

blocks.heading: Keep the A-sharp spelling
blocks.body: A# natural minor is A#, B#, C#, D#, E#, F#, and G#. Its signature has seven sharps, shared with C# major. B# and E# are intentional spellings. On a standard piano they use the physical C and F keys; a sharp in the written name does not guarantee a black key.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: The double-sharps have a purpose
blocks.body: A# harmonic minor raises G# to G##. Ascending classical melodic minor also raises F# to F##, giving A#-B#-C#-D#-E#-F##-G##-A#. Descending melodic minor returns through G# and F#. Keep the written G## and F## labels even though their piano keys sound as A and G in the keyboard mapping.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Read before following the hand diagram
blocks.body: For the reviewed melodic-minor left-hand example, the one-octave ascent starts with finger 3 on A#. The natural-minor left-hand ascent starts with finger 2 instead. The separate melodic descent is also recorded from its own diagram. Select the form before following finger numbers; these rows are not interchangeable.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A spelling-first practice task
blocks.body: Before playing, point to B#, E#, F##, and G## and name their physical keys. Then compare E#-F#-G##-A# with E#-F##-G##-A#. Return through A#-G#-F#-E# for the classical melodic descent. Write the note names once using double-sharp notation, then read your list without substituting a B-flat-minor spelling.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

/scales/b-major.title: B Major Piano Scale: Notes and Fingering
/scales/b-major.description: See B major notes, key signature, keyboard pitches and separately verified one-octave fingering for each hand and direction.
/scales/b-major.user_task: Learn B major’s five-sharp note set and its left-hand start on finger 4.
questions: What are the notes and key signature of B major?
Why does the left hand start B major with finger 4?
Which fingers are used by each hand ascending and descending over one octave?
What should I check during a short practice run?

blocks.heading: B Major notes
blocks.body: B Major contains B, C#, D#, E, F#, G#, A#. Repeat B at the top to complete one octave. Its key signature has 5 sharps.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Five sharps still leave E natural
blocks.body: B major uses five black keys, while B and E remain natural. The half-step pairs are D♯–E and A♯–B. Do not add an E-sharp just because this is a sharp key: E is the fourth degree in the verified note spelling.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Explanatory relationships derived from independently checked note spelling and the verified major-scale interval rule.

blocks.heading: One-octave fingering
blocks.body: This left-hand version begins B–C♯–D♯–E with 4–3–2–1. The thumb therefore reaches E before finger 4 crosses to F♯. The right hand begins with its thumb on B and uses 1–2–3–1–2–3–4–5. Each hand has its own starting finger.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A short practice check
blocks.body: Suggested drill: practice the left-hand opening four notes, then connect E to F♯ using 1–4. On the return, check F♯–E with 4–1. Complete one octave before increasing the range. Keep the B-major spelling in the staff and note labels even when comparing with an enharmonic scale.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Original suggested drill using only the source-verified notes and explicit fingering for this key. No effectiveness or fixed learning-time claim.

intervals.basis: Apply the verified major-scale interval rule to the independently checked note spelling. Descending order follows the same pitches from upper tonic to lower tonic.

display_register.RH: tonic written in octave 4 to tonic written in octave 5
display_register.LH: tonic written in octave 3 to tonic written in octave 4
display_register.basis: Editorial display choice; octave labels follow MusicXML C4=middle C; each accidental remains attached to its written octave. This register choice is not asserted to be a source-prescribed exercise range.

pitch_sequences.basis: MIDI = 12*(written_octave+1)+natural_letter_pitch_class+alter; computed from verified spelling. Cb4=59, equivalent to B3, not B4.

fingering.source_locator: LearnMusicTheory PDF page 1 B major row; Music Fun PDF page 8 staff
fingering.variant_note: A source-documented single-octave choice, not a claim that no alternative fingering is valid. Do not extend to multiple octaves by repeating these rows.
fingering.direction_evidence: Both ascending and descending notes and finger numbers were read directly in each displayed source staff; descending arrays were not merely assumed from an ascending-only source.

renderer_payload.tempo_status: editorial playback default; not a sourced examination speed or promised learning target
renderer_payload.source_of_truth: pitch_sequences plus same-hand fingering rows; no automatic enharmonic respelling

blocks.heading: B-Flat Major notes
blocks.body: B-Flat Major contains Bb, C, D, Eb, F, G, A. Repeat Bb at the top to complete one octave. Its key signature has 2 flats.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Two flats, two early thumb landings
blocks.body: B-flat and E-flat are the altered notes in B-flat major. D–E♭ and A–B♭ are its half-step pairs. The tonic is the black key B♭; it must keep that spelling in the note list and staff rather than being silently renamed A-sharp.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Explanatory relationships derived from independently checked note spelling and the verified major-scale interval rule.

blocks.heading: One-octave fingering
blocks.body: The source-selected right hand starts on B♭ with finger 2, places the thumb on C, and places it on F after E♭. It turns at the upper B♭ with finger 4. The left hand starts on finger 3 and turns at the upper B♭ with finger 2 in this documented single-octave version.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A short practice check
blocks.body: Suggested drill: play the right-hand pairs B♭–C and E♭–F with 2–1 and 3–1. Then rehearse the top A–B♭–A using 3–4–3 in the right hand and 1–2–1 in the left. Keep this selected fingering attached to its one-octave scope; do not extend it by simply repeating the row.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Original suggested drill using only the source-verified notes and explicit fingering for this key. No effectiveness or fixed learning-time claim.

intervals.basis: Apply the verified major-scale interval rule to the independently checked note spelling. Descending order follows the same pitches from upper tonic to lower tonic.

display_register.RH: tonic written in octave 4 to tonic written in octave 5
display_register.LH: tonic written in octave 3 to tonic written in octave 4
display_register.basis: Editorial display choice; octave labels follow MusicXML C4=middle C; each accidental remains attached to its written octave. This register choice is not asserted to be a source-prescribed exercise range.

pitch_sequences.basis: MIDI = 12*(written_octave+1)+natural_letter_pitch_class+alter; computed from verified spelling. Cb4=59, equivalent to B3, not B4.

fingering.source_locator: LearnMusicTheory PDF page 1 B-flat major row; Music Fun PDF page 11 staff
fingering.variant_note: A source-documented single-octave choice, not a claim that no alternative fingering is valid. Do not extend to multiple octaves by repeating these rows. Both checked PDFs choose LH finger 2 for the upper tonic turnaround. E-flat RH starts on 2 in these checked source examples. Preserve the source choice rather than silently normalizing it to another school.
fingering.direction_evidence: Both ascending and descending notes and finger numbers were read directly in each displayed source staff; descending arrays were not merely assumed from an ascending-only source.

/scales/g-minor.description: Find the notes of G minor, compare its three forms and descending patterns, and read source-checked piano fingerings.
/scales/g-minor.user_task: 直接查看指定调性的音阶、键位、手别指法和示范。
questions: What notes are in G natural minor?
Which notes change in G harmonic and melodic minor?
What is the descending classical melodic-minor sequence?
Which fingers are supported for each hand and range?
How do I match the keyboard, score and printed note names?

blocks.heading: Use B-flat and E-flat as the baseline
blocks.body: G natural minor contains G, A, Bb, C, D, Eb, and F. Its signature has Bb and Eb, shared with Bb major. Bb remains the third degree in all three minor forms here. Keep that note in place while comparing the changes nearer the upper G.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: F-sharp belongs to the harmonic form
blocks.body: G harmonic minor changes F to F# and keeps Eb. Ascending classical melodic minor also raises Eb to E natural, while melodic descent returns through F and Eb. The coexistence of Bb and F# is intentional. Each spelling shows its own degree in the G-minor scale.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Practice an ending without changing the opening
blocks.body: First locate G-A-Bb-C-D. Add Eb-F-G for natural minor, Eb-F#-G for harmonic minor, or E-F#-G for melodic ascent. Stop after each ending and identify it. For a return-trip check, choose a form before starting at the upper G, then read the descending sequence rather than relying on the ascent you just played.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.inference_basis: 本站编辑练习/实现建议；根据已核实的本调音名、上下行规则或明确指法行设计，未声称练习效果经实验验证。

blocks.heading: Rehearse the crossing in context
blocks.body: The sourced one-octave natural and harmonic ascents use right-hand finger 3 on Bb followed by the thumb on C. In the left-hand row, the thumb reaches D before finger 3 continues to Eb. Practice these connections separately, keeping the hand and selected form labels attached to your notes.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

/scales/chromatic.title: Chromatic Scale on Piano
/scales/chromatic.description: Read one-octave chromatic scales from C and G, including white-key half steps and alternative note spellings.
/scales/chromatic.user_task: Find every successive piano key in a chromatic octave and distinguish pitches from their written spellings.
questions: How many different pitches are in a chromatic octave?
Which white keys are already a half step apart?
Must ascending notes use sharps and descending notes use flats?
Does starting on G change the interval pattern?

blocks.heading: Every adjacent key
blocks.body: A chromatic scale moves through successive half steps. One octave contains twelve different pitch classes; the written exercise repeats the starting pitch at the top. On the keyboard, include both black and white keys. E to F and B to C are already half steps, so no black key is needed between either pair.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Start with the C example
blocks.body: The C example ascends through C, C-sharp, D, D-sharp, E, F, F-sharp, G, G-sharp, A, A-sharp, B and the next C. Check the two adjacent white-key pairs as you read. Every movement is the same size even when the pattern of black and white keys changes.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Different names can identify one key
blocks.body: Ascending sharp spellings and descending flat spellings are common, but they are not a universal rule. The displayed G example uses F for the key that the source names E-sharp. That is an editorial spelling choice; it does not change which key sounds. The descending examples use flats where appropriate for this reference.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

blocks.heading: Check the route in both directions
blocks.body: Read the C example upward, then return through every adjacent key. Next begin on G and compare the interval pattern. Keep the starting and ending notes visible. Use the written note names to check the route; finger numbers remain separate from note identification.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
