/scales/e-flat-major.title: E-Flat Major Piano Scale: Notes and Fingering
/scales/e-flat-major.description: See E-flat major notes, key signature, keyboard pitches and separately verified one-octave fingering for each hand and direction.
/scales/e-flat-major.user_task: Play E-flat major through its adjacent A-flat and B-flat notes and the following thumb crossing to C.
questions: What are the notes and key signature of E-flat major?
How do the right-hand fingers move from A-flat and B-flat to C?
Which fingers are used by each hand ascending and descending over one octave?
What should I check during a short practice run?

blocks.heading: E-Flat Major notes
blocks.body: E-Flat Major contains Eb, F, G, Ab, Bb, C, D. Repeat Eb at the top to complete one octave. Its key signature has 3 flats.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Keep the A-flat–B-flat pair together
blocks.body: E-flat major contains E♭, A♭, and B♭, with G–A♭ and D–E♭ as the half-step pairs. A♭ and B♭ are consecutive scale notes, but the distance between them is a whole step. The key signature lists the flats in the order B♭, E♭, A♭.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Explanatory relationships derived from independently checked note spelling and the verified major-scale interval rule.

blocks.heading: One-octave fingering
blocks.body: This one-octave source version starts the right hand with finger 2 on E♭. It assigns 3–4–1 to A♭–B♭–C and finishes on finger 3. The left hand starts E♭ with finger 3, crosses from G with the thumb to A♭ with finger 4, and turns at upper E♭ with finger 2.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: A short practice check
blocks.body: Suggested drill: play G–A♭–B♭–C in the right hand with 2–3–4–1, then return with 1–4–3–2. Follow this with a left-hand G–A♭ connection. Once those changes are clear, combine each fragment into a complete one-octave run while retaining the flat spellings.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.basis: Original suggested drill using only the source-verified notes and explicit fingering for this key. No effectiveness or fixed learning-time claim.

intervals.basis: Apply the verified major-scale interval rule to the independently checked note spelling. Descending order follows the same pitches from upper tonic to lower tonic.

display_register.RH: tonic written in octave 4 to tonic written in octave 5
display_register.LH: tonic written in octave 3 to tonic written in octave 4
display_register.basis: Editorial display choice; octave labels follow MusicXML C4=middle C; each accidental remains attached to its written octave. This register choice is not asserted to be a source-prescribed exercise range.

pitch_sequences.basis: MIDI = 12*(written_octave+1)+natural_letter_pitch_class+alter; computed from verified spelling. Cb4=59, equivalent to B3, not B4.

fingering.source_locator: LearnMusicTheory PDF page 1 E-flat major row; Music Fun PDF page 12 staff
fingering.variant_note: A source-documented single-octave choice, not a claim that no alternative fingering is valid. Do not extend to multiple octaves by repeating these rows. Both checked PDFs choose LH finger 2 for the upper tonic turnaround. E-flat RH starts on 2 in these checked source examples. Preserve the source choice rather than silently normalizing it to another school.
fingering.direction_evidence: Both ascending and descending notes and finger numbers were read directly in each displayed source staff; descending arrays were not merely assumed from an ascending-only source.

/scales/f-sharp-minor.title: F# Minor Scale on Piano: Natural, Harmonic & Melodic
/scales/f-sharp-minor.description: Find the notes of F# minor, compare its three forms and descending patterns, and read source-checked piano fingerings.
/scales/f-sharp-minor.user_task: 直接查看指定调性的音阶、键位、手别指法和示范。
questions: What notes are in F# natural minor?
Which notes change in F# harmonic and melodic minor?
What is the descending classical melodic-minor sequence?
Which fingers are supported for each hand and range?
How do I match the keyboard, score and printed note names?
Why does E# use the physical F key?

blocks.heading: Start with three sharps
blocks.body: F# natural minor is F#, G#, A, B, C#, D, and E. Its signature is shared with A major. F#, C#, and G# remain in the signature for each form. A stays natural throughout these minor versions, while the upper D and E are the changing degrees.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Write E-sharp, even on a white key
blocks.body: F# harmonic minor uses E# instead of E. Ascending classical melodic minor uses D# and E#. The classical melodic descent returns through E and D. E# is the seventh-degree spelling here; its physical piano key is F. Keep the displayed E# label in the score and note list rather than renaming it F.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Use the specified starting fingers
blocks.body: The sourced one-octave natural and harmonic ascents begin with right-hand finger 2 and left-hand finger 4 on F#. In the right hand, fingers 2-3 play F#-G# before the thumb plays A. Read the complete row for the selected hand. The melodic form requires its own reviewed row before finger numbers are offered.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Check the white-key leading note
blocks.body: Play C#-D-E-F#, then C#-D-E#-F#, then C#-D#-E#-F#. Say E-sharp before touching its white key. For the descending melodic check, begin at the upper F# and return through E-D-C#. Finish by writing the seventh degree for each form and matching it to the keyboard without changing its spelling.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]
blocks.inference_basis: 本站编辑练习/实现建议；根据已核实的本调音名、上下行规则或明确指法行设计，未声称练习效果经实验验证。

/arpeggios.title: Piano Arpeggios: C and G Major
/arpeggios.description: Find C and G major arpeggio notes, compare scales with chord tones, and use precisely scoped fingering examples.
/arpeggios.user_task: Understand an arpeggio and use the existing C/G major examples, including C scale versus arpeggio.
questions: What does arpeggio mean?
How does the C major arpeggio differ from its scale?
Which notes are in G major?
Which exact hand and octave does each fingering cover?

blocks.heading: Play the chord notes in sequence
blocks.body: An arpeggio presents chord tones one after another. This reference covers root-position C and G major triads. The C-major notes are C, E and G; the G-major notes are G, B and D. Repeating the root one octave higher gives a short ascending reference, followed here by the same notes descending.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: C major: scale and arpeggio
blocks.body: The C-major scale reads C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C. Its tonic arpeggio uses C, E, G, C: degrees 1, 3, 5 and the octave. Compare the two note rows before playing. The arpeggio skips the intervening scale notes instead of moving through each degree.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: G major: keep the triad in view
blocks.body: G major has F-sharp in its scale, but the G-major tonic triad contains G, B and D. The one-octave arpeggio is G, B, D, G. The scale and arpeggio share a key label while containing different numbers of distinct notes.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Read the scope of the finger numbers
blocks.body: The verified examples below cover C major in the right hand and G major in the left hand, each for one octave up and back. Their source prints every finger number. Follow the hand and register labels; these numbers are not a two-octave fingering chart. Other hand-specific examples remain to be checked.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实]

blocks.heading: Try one note check
blocks.body: Name the three chord tones, then read the short arpeggio upward and back. Compare it with the corresponding scale row. Work with one labeled hand example at a time, using the printed finger sequence only for its stated range.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断]

blocks.heading: Prepare before the first attempt
blocks.body: Basic reading can stop at each symbol. In this sight-reading activity, aim to carry an unfamiliar short line through a steady pulse. Check the clef, starting note, range, meter and longest or shortest note values before playing. This is an editorial practice procedure, not an exam test.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Use one attempt, then one observation
blocks.body: Count one empty bar and play Steps around middle C. Keep the beat through a mistake if you can. Afterwards, mark the bar that interrupted your pulse and study it separately. Once rehearsed, the line becomes reading practice; use a different line for another first attempt.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Read rhythm without pitch
blocks.body: Clap E-R1 while speaking 1 2 3 4, including the rests. E-R2 adds eighth-note subdivisions. Preview the silent beats before starting. The two rhythm lines are printed separately from the melody so you can work on timing alone.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Build C major
blocks.body: C–E–G is a C major triad. From C, E is four semitones higher and G is seven semitones higher. Find the three keys, play each once, then sound them together. Yamaha gives right-hand 1–3–5 as the usual root-position fingering for this example.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Change the middle note
blocks.body: Compare C–E–G with C–E♭–G. Lowering E by one semitone gives C minor. Compare the keyboard shapes and sound; the black key is E-flat in this chord’s spelling.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Practise a connection
blocks.body: Original exercise: play C4–E4–G4 for four counts, then C4–E4–A4 for four counts, and return. The second group is A minor in first inversion. C4 and E4 stay in place while G4 changes to A4. Plan the movement before counting in; use the chord chart to inspect each voicing. Fingering for this transition is not prescribed.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Choose an edition before a target speed
blocks.body: Look at the actual score: range, note values, hand changes and chord size matter more than the song title. Use the easy-song list to select a version and the sheet-music pages to check the exact edition. Begin with a phrase you can describe before playing.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Try the method on an original phrase
blocks.body: Use bars 1–2 of Steps around middle C. First speak C4 D4 E4, E4 D4 C4 while pointing to the notes. Clap each bar’s 1, 1, 2 duration pattern. Then play one bar, play the next, and join them without inserting a pause at the barline.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Build a connected run
blocks.body: Practise the join by starting one beat before the change. Add the next phrase only when you can explain what changes. For two-hand music, inspect each part separately before combining them. Save one slow continuous run for the end and write down the next small problem to solve.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

/guide/piano-scales.title: How to Practise Piano Scales
/guide/piano-scales.description: Start with one octave and one clear listening goal.
/guide/piano-scales.user_task: Use a scale reference to plan short, specific practice.
questions: Which scale can I start with?
When should I add the other hand?
What can I change when notes are uneven?

blocks.heading: Choose a small starting set
blocks.body: Editorial starting order: C major, then G major, then F major. C uses white keys; G introduces F-sharp and F introduces B-flat. This is one learning route, not a universal difficulty ranking. Open each scale’s own chart and verified fingering before playing.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Separate the tasks
blocks.body: Name the scale notes first. Play one octave with one hand, pause, then check the return journey. Use the exact ascending and descending fingering shown in the selected chart; do not reverse or extend a number pattern by assumption. Add the other hand separately before trying hands together.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Make one useful change
blocks.body: Original five-minute plan: one minute naming C D E F G A B C; two minutes checking each hand slowly; one minute on a single uneven crossing; one minute playing and listening again. If the crossing rushes, pause before it in the isolated exercise, then restore an even pulse. This timing is a sample allocation, not a required daily dose.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

original_demo.name: Name then play one octave
original_demo.fingering: use verified data there; no new inferred sequence

common_problems.action: Check F-sharp in the scale reference before restarting.
Isolate the join; choose a slower even pulse.
Return to separate hands, then join a shorter segment.

blocks.heading: Start with a repeatable rhythm
blocks.body: Our original Four-bar sketch uses a one-beat, one-beat, two-beat pattern for three bars. Its melody changes with C, F and G harmony, then ends over C. Play the melody alone first; the supplied lower chord notes are an optional accompaniment.

blocks.heading: Make one variation

blocks.heading: Write enough information to replay it

blocks.heading: Check the exact book

blocks.heading: Select rather than race through
blocks.body: With a teacher, select a short passage that addresses an observed issue, such as an uneven rhythm or an unclear release. Read that edition’s notes and finger numbers before repeating it. Keep the excerpt small enough to notice a change; a speed target alone does not define success.

blocks.heading: Use an observable check
blocks.body: Editorial practice card: identify one bar, state one listening goal, play it slowly, pause, and compare the next attempt. Stop when the hand becomes uncomfortable or tense and reset with your teacher. No claim is made that repetitions prevent injury or guarantee strength.

/guide/note-values-and-rhythm.title: Note Values and Rhythm
/guide/note-values-and-rhythm.description: Read how long to play, how long to rest and how to count a bar.
/guide/note-values-and-rhythm.user_task: Decode basic duration symbols and perform original rhythm exercises.
questions: How long is each note?
What do dots and ties do?
How do 4/4 and 6/8 differ?

blocks.heading: Use a stated beat unit
blocks.body: In these 4/4 exercises, a quarter note lasts one beat: whole 4, half 2, eighth 1/2 and sixteenth 1/4. Corresponding rests use the same durations but leave silence. These beat counts depend on the chosen beat unit; a whole note does not fill every possible meter.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Add duration carefully
blocks.body: A dot adds half the undotted value, so a dotted quarter lasts 1.5 quarter-note units. A tie joins two notes of the same pitch into one sustained duration; do not strike the second note again. A slur is a different instruction.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Count the subdivision
blocks.body: For E-R2 say 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &. The first bar starts with two eighth notes, then a quarter and a half. In compound 6/8, six eighth-note units are normally grouped into two dotted-quarter beats: ONE-and-a TWO-and-a. Keep that grouping distinct from the four quarter-note beats in our 4/4 lines.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Clap, then check
blocks.body: Try the printed rhythm lines without looking at their answer counts. Keep counting during rests. After one attempt, check that each 4/4 bar totals four quarter-note units and mark any attack that arrived early or late.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Choose the problem first

blocks.heading: Keep the feedback specific

blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Finish with a transfer

/guide/piano-hand-position.title: Piano Hand Position and Sitting Setup
/guide/piano-hand-position.description: Set up your seat, let the arms move and avoid forcing a fixed hand shape.
/guide/piano-hand-position.user_task: Check a comfortable starting posture using a simple diagram.
questions: How high should I sit?
How should fingers and wrists look?
Which common ideas are misleading?

blocks.heading: Set up before playing
blocks.body: Sit near the front of a stable bench, facing the keyboard. Support your feet. Adjust your height so your elbows are approximately level with the keys, with shoulders and arms relaxed. Reach the keyboard without lifting the shoulders.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Let the hand remain mobile
blocks.body: Use gently curved fingers and a wrist that continues the general line of the forearm. The side-view diagram is a starting reference, not a fixed angle to hold throughout a piece. Key position and musical movement change how the hand travels.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Check a single note
blocks.body: Place a hand over a small group of keys, play one note and release. Notice whether the shoulder rises or the wrist locks. Pause and reset if the action feels forced. Avoid treating “curved fingers” as an instruction to claw tightly or “level wrist” as an instruction never to move.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

/guide/piano-practice.title: Plan a Useful Piano Practice Session
/guide/piano-practice.description: Give each part of practice a small goal and leave a clear next step.
/guide/piano-practice.user_task: Choose a short plan matched to a current goal.
questions: What should I practise today?
How can a short session be organised?
How do I decide what to do next?

blocks.heading: A ten-minute beginner plan
blocks.body: Use two minutes to find the starting notes, three to clap and read a phrase, three to play and join two sections, and two for a continuous attempt and a written note. Treat these times as an editable example, not a minimum requirement.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: A twenty-minute developing-player plan
blocks.body: Spend three minutes on one scale issue, five on an unfamiliar reading line, eight on one passage from your piece, and four on a familiar section and a brief log. Choose material at a manageable level so the goals stay observable.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Write a useful next step
blocks.body: Replace “practise more” with a concrete observation such as “count through the rest in bar 3.” Record what improved and what still interrupted the phrase. The final page of the starter pack has a printable session checklist.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

/guide/music-symbols-and-piano-terms.user_task: Interpret common notation and performance words without mixing them with instrument names.
questions: What does piano mean on a score?
How do note symbols and performance words differ?
How should I interpret repeat directions?

blocks.heading: Piano on a score means soft
blocks.body: As a dynamic instruction, piano, abbreviated p, means soft. It does not ask for a different instrument. The nearby musical context tells you where the dynamic begins and how it relates to surrounding markings.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Read symbols by their job
blocks.body: A clef sets the pitch reference, an accidental changes a written pitch, and a note or rest value gives duration. A dot beside a note adds duration; a staccato dot above or below a note asks for separation. Position matters.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

blocks.heading: Follow the whole instruction
blocks.body: D.C. asks for a return to the beginning; D.S. asks for a return to the segno. A following al Fine tells you to end at Fine after that return. Read the full direction and its destination together. Tempo words such as allegro do not specify one universal metronome number.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] factual core; [推断] editorial exercise/method where stated

terms.example: Play the marked phrase loudly, with control.
Use a softer dynamic than p in this passage.
Increase loudness across the marked span.
Reduce loudness across the marked span.
Treat the tempo word as context, not one fixed BPM.
Choose the pulse in the context of the piece.
Use the score or edition for a metronome indication.
Shorten the marked note without deleting its place in the rhythm.
Assign the marked passage to the right hand.
Assign the marked passage to the left hand.
Return to the beginning when instructed.
Stop here after the relevant return instruction.

symbols.meaning: lower written pitch by a semitone

symbols.meaning: cancel the applicable sharp or flat

claims.statement_zh: 本批major triad的根音以上半音偏移为0、4、7；minor triad为0、3、7。
Am为A-C-E三和弦；三个密集排列为A-C-E、C-E-A、E-A-C。
Am/C以C为低音，Am/E以E为低音；根音仍为A。
claims.derivation: 将已核实的A-C-E及转位低音/斜线命名规则应用到两个排列；不是按根音总在最下面的简化描述生成。

claims.statement_zh: 同根大小三和弦的三音相差一个半音，根音和五音保持。
C4表示中央C；Cb4与B3对应同一琴键，书写拼写不能直接替换。
本包采用十二平均律、A4=440Hz且MIDI69的音高约定。
音符MIDI编号与频率由书写音名及公式换算；具体八度和播放时长是本批展示选择。
Am的本批三种排列均只使用白键。
claims.derivation: 已核实A/C/E；在键盘音级布局中均为自然音白键，换八度不会改变键色。

claims.statement_zh: Cb-Eb-Gb与B-D#-F#在本包十二平均律键盘中对应相同键位；仍保持两个和弦名称。
Am7比Am三和弦增加G；本包未制作七和弦工具数据。
claims.derivation: S01小七和弦=小三和弦加小七度；A之上小七度为G。这里只解释符号区别，不将历史Am7线索并入关键词表。

claims.statement_zh: 十二平均律每八度12个半音音高，12不表示钢琴总共只有12个和弦。
claims.derivation: 把每八度12个根音位置与每个根音可构成多种和弦品质区别；不将本批9个命名和弦宣称为全量。

claims.statement_zh: 本批root-position音区、示范时长、步骤顺序和图表收录顺序为原创编辑选择。
claims.derivation: 为两页真实排版和复现所选，不是学习效果、最优指法或流行度结论。

claims.statement_zh: C major组成音为C–E–G。
A minor组成音为A–C–E。
A major组成音为A–C#–E。
C minor组成音为C–Eb–G。
G major组成音为G–B–D。
E major组成音为E–G#–B。
A-flat major组成音为Ab–C–Eb。
B major组成音为B–D#–F#。
C-flat major组成音为Cb–Eb–Gb。
